papers.title: Intrinsic Distribution Matching

summary.tldr: Intrinsic Distribution Matching (IDM) enhances diffusion distillation by combining reverse-KL score matching with explicit moment constraints on feature means and standard deviations computed from the generator's EMA copy.
key_points: Decomposes the reverse-KL vector field into a Gaussian moment component and a non-Gaussian residual to identify explicit statistics for constraints.
Matches feature means and per-coordinate standard deviations using the generator's EMA copy, eliminating the need for an external feature encoder like DINOv2.
Uses internal velocity branches to estimate score differences instead of relying on a separate fake-score network.
Evaluated via full-parameter and LoRA tuning on Z-Image-Turbo 6B and Qwen-Image 20B models.
summary.why_it_matters: IDM achieves state-of-the-art text rendering performance on LongText-Bench at two network function evaluations without requiring auxiliary external encoders.

papers.title: A-RSI: Adaptive Task Refresh for Zero-Data Multimodal Self-Improvement

summary.tldr: A-RSI enables zero-data multimodal self-improvement by using training dynamics to adaptively refresh a pool of programmatically generated tasks without external data or test-set access.
key_points: Monitors training log metrics, specifically reward variation and accuracy, to detect declining learning signals and trigger task refreshes without consulting validation or test scores.

Generates multimodal questions and reference answers autonomously using a static library of model-authored programs and independently checkable targets, avoiding reliance on self-consistency or majority voting.
Achieves an increase in average performance from 57.77 to 61.05 across an eleven-benchmark suite after adding 800 fresh tasks.
Includes automated verification of reward and refresh rule properties, alongside separate audits of generated reference answers.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that vision-language models can continuously self-improve without human labels, external datasets, or validation leakages by algorithmically managing their own task refresh cycles.

papers.title: Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs

summary.tldr: LOWN is a training-free decoding method for Diffusion Vision-Language Models that reduces FLOPs by skipping visual token processing whenever image-free predictions match previous image-conditioned outputs.
key_points: Analysis of LLaDA-V shows visual tokens account for 89-97% of inputs, but removing the image alters token unmasking at only 22.8% of decoding steps on average (and as few as 7.9%).
LOWN predicts masked tokens without the image first, only reprocessing visual tokens when predictions disagree with the last image-conditioned state, using agreement to certify tokens for unmasking.
LOWN adapts dynamically across benchmarks without manual threshold tuning, maintaining 99.6% of LLaDA-V's baseline accuracy while requiring only 35.3% of decoding FLOPs on average.
The method generalizes across LLaDA-based DVLMs, integrates orthogonally with visual token pruning techniques, and supports key-value caching.
summary.why_it_matters: It drastically cuts inference computational overhead in diffusion VLMs without requiring model retraining, fine-tuning, or performance tradeoffs.

papers.title: L3G-World: Real-Time Infinite World Generation with Latent 3D Gaussian Memory

summary.tldr: L3G-World enables real-time 9 FPS infinite world generation using a Latent 3D Gaussian Memory that updates with scene extent rather than stream length.
key_points: Latent 3D Gaussian Memory (L3G) stores VAE latent features directly on 3D Gaussians, allowing rendering straight into a Video Diffusion Transformer's (DiT) latent space without VAE re-encoding.
The framework alternates autoregressively between a memory updater and a video DiT, spawning new Gaussians for unobserved areas while refining existing ones.
Memory complexity scales with spatial scene extent instead of temporal stream length, reducing 3D primitive count up to 38.6x compared to prior 3D-memory baselines.
Achieves performance improvements including up to 3.2x faster memory updates and 359x faster memory rendering over existing baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: By removing VAE re-encoding bottlenecks and decoupling memory growth from stream length, the architecture achieves 9 FPS real-time generation of spatially consistent, long-horizon interactive 3D environments.

papers.title: WorkFactory: Turning Professional Intents into Executable Work for Scalable Agent Training

summary.tldr: WorkFactory is a scalable framework that uses information support graphs and probe executions to construct 112,686 executable professional tasks across 612 occupations for training working agents.
key_points: Uses information-level planning to construct an information support graph that explicitly maps data dependencies and locations for intended outputs.
Executes probes to detect environment support failures and guide task repairs while maintaining original work intents.
Trains the WorkPilot model family (Qwen 4B, 27B, and 35B-A3B) on collected teacher trajectories, boosting WorkPilot-35B-A3B Elo from 879 to 1565 on GDPval-AA v2.1.
Reveals model-dependent diminishing returns where agent execution length initially increases and subsequently decreases during scaling.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides an automated methodology to fix defective task environments and generate massive, reliable demonstration datasets for training AI agents on complex real-world occupations.

papers.title: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers

summary.tldr: SpecSlot is a pixel-space rectified-flow Transformer that decouples spectral detail from global attention sequence length by expanding spatial anchors into frequency-specific slots that interact locally.
key_points: Expands spatial anchors into multiple slots assigned to disjoint bands of Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) coefficients.
Restricts global attention to the lowest-frequency slot per anchor, while all slots interact locally to prevent sequence length inflation.
Employs a spatial head to apply local corrections to spectral predictions, retaining pixel-space generative states, targets, and losses.
Outperforms JiT controls on ImageNet-512 with a 2.84 FID improvement at 3.9% fewer FLOPs, and beats JiT-B/8 on DPG-Bench by 1.06 with 40.6% lower forward cost.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables generative Transformers to scale up fine-grained spatial and spectral visual details without incurring the quadratic computational costs of long global attention sequences.

papers.title: Co-Design Bench: Multimodal Collaborative Coding Evaluation for Agentic Models

summary.tldr: Co-Design Bench is a reference-free benchmark containing 273 multimodal tasks and 2,331 hidden criteria to evaluate agentic models on real-user application editing.
key_points: Tasks are derived from 37,463 deduplicated queries across 26,314 real sessions and split into Multimodal Editing (ME) and Repository Editing (RE) tracks.
Evaluation relies on a judge-then-refute protocol that uses source and browser evidence to verify claims without relying on gold code or target screenshots.
The top-performing model endpoint achieved an average criterion pass rate of 69.9% per task, but only fully solved 26.4% of complete tasks.
Across all ten evaluated endpoints, criterion completion rates dropped when repository edits spanned three or four change types compared to one or two.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a realistic, execution-based standard for evaluating how effectively AI agents convert complex multimodal user feedback into fully functional codebases.

papers.title: HairDeck: Animation-Ready Stylized Hair Cards from a Single Image

summary.tldr: HairDeck is a set diffusion transformer that generates animation-ready stylized hair cards and spring-bone chains from a single image.
key_points: Treats a card hairstyle as an unordered set where each hair card is represented as a single token.
Uses a set diffusion transformer to denoise all hair cards simultaneously, replacing autoregressive sequential decoding.
Generates both the hair card geometry and the corresponding spring-bone chains for animation driving.
Reduces Chamfer distance by 44% and card-orientation error by over 50% compared to CHARM.
Executes 33 times faster than CHARM on its own test set.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables rapid creation of fully animatable stylized 3D character hair assets from a single input image for games and avatars.

papers.title: WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One Agent From Narration to Long-Form Video

summary.tldr: WeVisCut introduces a 9B single-agent policy and harness for long-form script-to-video editing that matches Claude Opus 5 performance while using 33x fewer generated tokens per successful output minute.
key_points: Uses a shared production state harness that enables tool feedback to guide subsequent editing decisions and error repairs.
Features a four-stage data pipeline combining editing inversion and verified replay, extracting over 130K training examples from 3,750 finished videos.
Trains a single 9B model policy to coordinate full video production and failure recovery within the harness.
Evaluated on a new 100-task benchmark using five metrics for editing quality and delivery reliability, outperforming task-matched native editors.
summary.why_it_matters: It proves that a compact, task-adapted 9B model can achieve frontier-level video editing quality at a fraction of the computational and token cost of large generalist LLMs.

papers.title: IntReal: A Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for Multimodal Interleaved Generation

summary.tldr: IntReal introduces IntReal-100K, a real-world multimodal interleaved dataset, along with a fine-grained, seven-dimension evaluation suite that achieves strong human agreement and low redundancy for benchmarking Unified Multimodal Models.
key_points: IntReal-100K provides a real-world interleaved dataset spanning four major categories to address the lack of specialized multimodal generation training data.

The IntReal Evaluation Suite diagnoses performance across seven complementary dimensions using expert models, demonstrating low pairwise metric redundancy (Spearman's ρ ≤ 0.42) and high agreement with human judgments (83.3% accuracy).
Evaluator consistency across different expert models is high, exhibiting a Spearman's ρ > 0.9.
Post-training experiments confirm that IntReal-100K enhances interleaved generation and reveal that unimodal generation training directly benefits multimodal interleaved performance.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a standardized benchmark for interleaved generation and demonstrates that models can be improved via modality-specific optimization rather than relying strictly on joint text-image training.

papers.title: PhysInsert: Physically Plausible Object Insertion with Geometric Priors and Bidirectional Object-Scene Interactions

summary.tldr: PhysInsert is a framework for physically plausible object insertion that utilizes VGGT geometry streams and 2D spatial supervision to jointly adapt object pose, illumination, and scene interactions using a novel Blender-rendered dataset.
key_points: Introduces the Insert World dataset containing Blender-rendered counterfactual pairs and object references with aligned viewpoints and lighting conditions.
Uses Geometry-Guided Adaptation, combining a VGGT geometry stream with image and text streams supervised by target-scene features to maintain spatial consistency.
Employs 2D Object-Scene Spatial Supervision to simultaneously supervise object occupancy and environmental changes while grounding text instructions using image-text attention.
Evaluates performance on PhysInsert-Bench, a new benchmark tailored for cross-environment and cross-view object insertion requiring illumination and pose adaptation.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables more realistic synthetic image editing and composition by ensuring inserted objects automatically match the perspective, pose, and lighting of the target environment.

papers.title: WebAnything: From the Wild Web to Scalable Agent Environments

summary.tldr: WebAnything is a fully automated framework that reconstructs source-grounded, reusable web environments from real URLs using an Explorer-Builder and an independent verifier, eliminating per-site manual setup and repairs.
key_points: Uses an Explorer-Builder to collect browser-observable structures, resources, and interaction outcomes, alongside an independent verifier for local repair and targeted recapture.
Generates 244 website artifacts across 14 application domains and 53 categories, supporting 12,984 executed and accepted tasks.
Outperforms human-assisted WebHarbor across three fidelity metrics with 12 wins, two ties, and zero losses in a blind audit.
Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-9B on 5,856 interaction trajectories increases REAL success by 9.9 percentage points and WebArena-Verified Overall success by 13.33 percentage points.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables scalable, reproducible training and evaluation of web agents by automatically converting real-world websites into executable environments without manual engineering.

papers.title: Glance: The Generator Is Its Own Reranker

summary.tldr: Glance unifies reranking and generation into a single resident 9B model using a lightweight decision adapter and pointer head to score candidate passages from a shared prefill.
key_points: Uses short relevance probes branching from cached context to score candidates without separate query-passage prefills, scaling up to 200 candidates (43k tokens).
Adds approximately 0.1 GiB of memory per decision skill to a single 9B parameter backbone model.
Achieves nDCG@10 of 0.741 on SciFact and 0.345 on NFCorpus after 39 minutes of MS MARCO fine-tuning, outperforming bge-reranker-v2-m3 (0.721 and 0.326).
Improves downstream answer F1 by 0.045 over cross-encoder-selected context on 300 HotpotQA questions while enabling generation to continue from the existing passage cache.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the need to host and run separate models for reranking and generation in RAG pipelines, significantly reducing latency, GPU memory overhead, and redundant processing.

papers.title: AskStream: When and What to Ask Proactively under Uncertainty in Streaming Video Understanding

summary.tldr: AskStream is a streaming video benchmark introducing an 'ask' action to help multimodal models actively request missing information under video or user uncertainty.
key_points: Redefines the proactive video understanding paradigm by adding an 'ask' action alongside the traditional 'wait' and 'answer' choices.
Comprises a benchmark of 438 streaming videos featuring 2,714 manually annotated frame-level time windows across four task categories and eight subtasks.
Evaluates models using a proposed Ask-F1 metric across both multiple-choice and open-ended interaction settings.
Top-performing models achieve only 52.18% Ask-F1, indicating significant limitations in current MLLM capabilities for proactive information seeking.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a standard for evaluating proactive agents that must clarify ambiguous user queries or incomplete video inputs instead of waiting indefinitely or hallucinating responses.

papers.title: EditAgent: Rethinking Agentic Image Editing

summary.tldr: EditAgent improves agentic image editing by expanding the action space with specialized tools and enhancing the observation space with structured verification records for parallel listwise judging.
key_points: Identifies key limitations in current agentic editors: over 40% failure rates for general-purpose editors on expert benchmarks and lack of a universally reliable judge.
Expands action and observation spaces by combining general editors with specialized methods and generating structured verification records for each candidate output.
Replaces sequential refinement with parallel candidate generation and a single listwise VLM judge call, enabling off-the-shelf VLMs to outperform finetuned reward models.
Achieves a 78.5% win rate in human expert preference over sequential approaches while reducing total judge calls by at least 50%.
Serves as an effective data engine to enhance two open-weight editors across three evaluation benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that combining specialized tool routing with parallel candidate verification significantly cuts compute costs and improves quality over traditional sequential refinement in vision-language tasks.

papers.title: Rethinking Neural Thickets Without Weight Perturbations

summary.tldr: Researchers debunk the Neural Thickets weight-geometry hypothesis, demonstrating that its gains stem from output diversity, validation-based selection, and voting, which can be matched using a training-free logit perturbation method called PSV.
key_points: Perturbing a single decoder block recovers most performance gains, while adding random bias directly to output logits of a fully frozen model matches or exceeds full-weight perturbations on reasoning tasks.
Formalized the Perturb-Select-Vote (PSV) framework, which generates perturbed predictors, selects top performers using a small validation set, and aggregates their predictions at inference time.
First-order mathematical analysis reveals that small weight perturbations function primarily by inducing downstream logit shifts rather than accessing distinct weight-space experts.

Applied logit PSV to computer vision, achieving substantial performance improvements under domain shifts (including Earth observation data) where full-weight perturbations offered minimal added benefit.
summary.why_it_matters: Logit PSV provides a simple, computation-light, training-free alternative to weight-perturbation ensembles across language and vision models without requiring model weight modifications.

papers.title: SCARL: Sequence Confidence-Aligned Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: SCARL reshapes reinforcement learning advantages using sequence-confidence alignment gaps, preventing entropy collapse and improving language-model reasoning without requiring extra forward/backward passes.
key_points: Identifies sequence-confidence misalignment in RLVR, where confidence level does not scale the gradient update magnitude relative to error or certainty.
Reshapes advantage magnitude without changing its sign using the gap between group-relative confidence and outcome, normalized by class advantage budgets.
Provably reduces to the base advantage estimator when confidence within a class is uniform, introducing only one hyperparameter and zero additional passes.
Outperforms nine compute-matched methods on Qwen3-4B-Base, improving average Pass@32 by 2.4 points over DAPO and boosting performance in 14 of 16 tested estimator/backbone settings.
summary.why_it_matters: SCARL enhances policy optimization in verifiable reasoning tasks by preventing premature entropy collapse and better separating correct from incorrect responses across diverse RL estimators.

papers.title: How to Loop Your Transformer: Loop Scaling, Specialization, and Parallel Inference

summary.tldr: A comprehensive study on dense decoder-only transformers reveals that looping strategies must align with parameter or training FLOP constraints, and introduces adapter specialization and modified parallel looping to improve quality and inference speed.
key_points: Full-transformer looping yields the best performance for fixed parameter budgets, while looping middle layer blocks is optimal under training FLOP constraints.
Looping quality eventually saturates or becomes unstable; adding small loop-specific low-rank adapters recovers performance gains as loop counts scale up to 32.
Parallel Loop Transformers enable concurrent loop execution across adjacent tokens, but require preserving current-token embeddings and separately normalizing combined states to maintain quality.
summary.why_it_matters: Designing looped transformers according to specific compute constraints and architecture modifications allows practitioners to scale model depth and inference throughput without increasing parameter counts.

papers.title: Distributional Reward Calibration and Budget-Neutral Credit Assignment for Multimodal RLVR

summary.tldr: TACE improves GRPO advantage estimation through optimal-transport reward standardization and budget-neutral token credit assignment.
key_points: GRPO advantage estimation is factorized into sample-level baselining and token-level credit assignment.
Stage 1 uses a 1D optimal-transport map to a standard normal distribution to normalize task reward laws and bound outlier gradients deterministically.
Stage 2 applies a rank-calibrated stop-gradient evidence contrast renormalized to mean one, conserving total credit mass and sign across trajectory tokens.
Theoretical guarantees include population-level inter-task moment equity, deterministic tail bounds, mass conservation, boundedness, and sign-anchoring.
Evaluations on a multimodal reasoning suite demonstrate top performance on the majority of benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: TACE prevents heavy-tailed reward outliers and unconstrained token updates from destabilizing reinforcement learning from verifier rewards (RLVR) in multimodal models.

papers.title: An ODE-based Sampler for Discrete Diffusion Models

summary.tldr: Exponential residual flows (ERFs) introduce a deterministic, ODE-based sampling framework for discrete diffusion models by augmenting discrete tokens with continuous residual variables.
key_points: Augments each discrete token and position with a continuous residual variable that evolves deterministically via piecewise-defined ODEs.
Triggers discrete state transitions whenever a continuous residual variable reaches zero.
Uses vector fields dependent on the discrete state and the forward and backward rate matrices to prove exact marginal preservation of the original diffusion.
Provides specialized discretizations for masked and uniform diffusion that enable consistency distillation.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables deterministic probability flow sampling and consistency distillation in discrete diffusion models, leading to faster sampling and improved performance in text and code generation.

papers.title: Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm

summary.tldr: A unified framework replaces the multi-stage training pipeline by deriving RL objectives as maximum-likelihood fitting to model-generated target distributions, training foundation models with a single likelihood-based algorithm.
key_points: Derives reinforcement learning objectives as maximum-likelihood fitting to model-generated target distributions.
Unifies pretraining, midtraining, SFT, and RL into a single trainer that mixes static data and model generations.
Frame the training lifecycle around data selection, proportions, and scheduling, treating staged training as a special case.
Demonstrates improved accuracy-compute tradeoffs, better task coverage, capability preservation, and enhanced continual learning.
summary.why_it_matters: It simplifies the foundation model post-training infrastructure and improves compute efficiency by replacing disparate training algorithms with a single likelihood-based system.

papers.title: Preserving Utility in Continual LLM Unlearning via Orthogonal Projections

summary.tldr: Continual Orthogonal Projection (COP) prevents model degradation during sequential LLM unlearning by restricting gradient updates to the orthogonal complement of low-rank activation subspaces cached from previous forget sets.
key_points: Addresses utility and forgetting decay caused by gradient interference across sequential deletion requests.
Provides a provable theoretical guarantee of first-order non-interference with past unlearning operations.
Stores only a low-rank activation basis per layer, avoiding the need to retain past gradients or raw forget data.
Integrates into existing gradient-based differentiable loss unlearning methods without altering their loss objectives.
Demonstrates superior utility preservation and unlearning efficacy on the TOFU and RWKU benchmarks compared to standard and continual baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: COP enables long-term compliance with data removal requests (such as privacy or copyright enforcement) in deployed LLMs without causing performance collapse or requiring costly retraining from scratch.

papers.title: Latent Path Exploration via Potential-Guided Subtrajectory Balance

summary.tldr: SubLAT improves stochastic continuous latent reasoning in language models by coupling a relative answer potential with Subtrajectory Balance to guide intermediate transition paths.
key_points: SubLAT introduces a relative answer potential to evaluate answer support of sampled intermediate latent states against replacement states using terminal correctness signals.
Employs Subtrajectory Balance to relate potential differences across varying subtrajectory lengths to forward and backward transition densities.
Trains models via joint optimization of answer supervision, Chain-of-Thought (CoT) supervision, and representation distillation.
Demonstrates increased solution coverage with higher sampling budgets and improved performance on structural out-of-domain (OOD) arithmetic and deductive reasoning tasks.
Trajectory analysis confirms progressive path divergence and higher mean relative potentials for correct reasoning paths.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables language models to effectively explore complex, multi-path reasoning spaces in continuous latent representations without producing explicit token traces.

papers.title: Elucidating the Design Space of LM Data Attribution

summary.tldr: The CATT benchmark isolates LM data attribution failures, revealing that negative log-odds gradients and top-token aggregation significantly improve attribution recall over standard document-averaging cross-entropy methods.
key_points: Introduces the Controlled Attribution Benchmark (CATT), using fictitious knowledge fine-tuning to provide unambiguous ground-truth for systematically testing dataset properties like document redundancy and lexical distractors.
Shows that true causal evidence in training documents is highly localized, and standard document-wide token score averaging dilutes this evidence into noise.
Replaces standard cross-entropy loss gradients with negative log-odds gradients to isolate critical target tokens from uninformative ones.
Aggregating only top-token scores increases ground truth recall by 35 to 72 percentage points across multiple baselines on CATT.
Demonstrates transferability to FTRACE-TREX, improving counterfactual retraining performance across all tested attribution methods by up to 4.9x.
summary.why_it_matters: Simple changes to loss gradient formulation and token aggregation can dramatically improve the accuracy of tracing specific outputs back to training data without inventing new estimators.

papers.title: Multi-View MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation

summary.tldr: Multi-View MoE uses multiple independent routers to aggregate expert scores and dynamically mix latent input views for expert computation without increasing the active-expert budget.
key_points: Multi-Router aggregates sigmoid scores from independently initialized routers to resolve weak agreement between single-router rankings and actual expert utility.
Latent input views are mixed into each expert's input using the relative routing scores across the routers, allowing routing preferences to modulate computation.
Each selected expert performs a single forward pass, keeping active-expert count, expert FLOPs, and all-to-all communication volume identical to standard MoE.
Evaluated on a 24-layer 10B-A1B model (708B tokens), Multi-View MoE increased the nine-task downstream mean score by 1.18 percentage points over the baseline.
Multi-Router alone improved downstream performance by 0.6 percentage points and increased global rank correlation between router scores and expert utility by 8.1%.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves MoE routing accuracy and downstream performance at zero additional FLOP or communication cost per active expert.

security.title: Difficulty Calibration Across Time for Membership Inference in Diffusion Models

summary.tldr: New membership inference attacks calibrate diffusion model loss using two time dimensions: Reference-Model Calibration across training time checkpoints and Temporal Self-Calibration across diffusion timesteps within a single model.
key_points: Reference-Model Calibration (RMC) isolates newly memorized data by comparing a fine-tuned model's loss against an earlier checkpoint.
Temporal Self-Calibration (TSC) operates on a single model by comparing loss at a target diffusion timestep against neighboring timesteps to filter inherent image difficulty from true memorization.
Both methods beat state-of-the-art MIA performance and generalize across x-, v-, and ε-prediction model parameterizations without requiring text captions.
summary.why_it_matters: These methods enable highly accurate privacy auditing and copyright detection for diffusion models across various architecture types, even without access to auxiliary reference models or captions.

security.title: The Privacy and Security Risks of Edge LLM Optimization

summary.tldr: Edge LLM optimization creates security drift and new attack surfaces by altering representations, decision pathways, and trust boundaries despite preserving task performance.
key_points: Deploying Large Language Models on edge devices requires optimization to reduce memory, computation, and energy demands.
Task performance preservation during optimization does not guarantee the preservation of underlying model security.
Optimization acts as an information transformation that modifies model representations and internal decision pathways.
summary.why_it_matters: Edge LLM compression and acceleration techniques can unknowingly introduce vulnerabilities and compromise model security without altering benchmark task accuracy.

security.title: Understanding and Mitigating Role Spoofing in LLMs

summary.tldr: Researchers identify role spoofing in LLMs via combined structural and semantic prompt injections, explaining why adversarial safety training fails against it and proposing a linear probe detection method.
key_points: LLMs track conversational roles using both content cues (semantics, writing style) and structural cues (control tokens, formatting).
Role spoofing occurs when malicious tool outputs (e.g., untrusted webpages) impersonate the user by combining fake structural and content cues.
Adversarial training focused on ignoring content-based injections leaves LLMs vulnerable to structure-based spoofing, explaining frontier model susceptibility.
A mitigation method using linear probes trained to predict conversational roles effectively detects role spoofing across multiple settings.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding role spoofing helps developers prevent indirect prompt injections in autonomous LLM agents that process untrusted web data.

security.title: Surprise Alone Learns Lies: Evidence-Gated Continual Learning for LLMs from Streaming Claims

summary.tldr: A study demonstrates that surprise-driven continual learning in LLMs selectively absorbs lies and evaluates mechanisms like model priors, LLM judges, and evidence retrieval to gate stream updates.
key_points: Surprise-driven selection absorbs planted falsehoods at rates similar to random selection because low-probability claims are highly surprising by design.

The model's original prior distinguishes lies about known facts from true new facts (AUC 0.78-0.83 across Qwen2.5-1.5B, Qwen2.5-3B, and Llama-3.2-3B), but fails to separate lies from legitimate updates (AUC 0.53).
Filtering with model priors saves 43% of LLM judge calls, but white-box attackers can craft lies that bypass prior-based filters.

Routing contradicted claims to trusted evidence sources lowers the poison rate among learned claims, but performance degrades below judge-only baselines if an attacker plants matching sources for 30% of lies.
summary.why_it_matters: Naively selecting stream inputs based on model surprise makes continual learning pipelines highly vulnerable to data poisoning and hallucination uptake.

security.title: InferD: A Honeypot Framework for AI Inference Infrastructure

summary.tldr: InferD is a low-interaction honeypot framework for exposed AI inference infrastructure that operates on the principle of deception without inference.
key_points: Operates on a 'deception without inference' design where every observable response comes from static pools, avoiding actual model inference or tool execution.
Emulates key observable behaviors of AI serving stacks, including model inventories, token formats, tool-call protocols, and authorization flows.
Decomposes AI system emulation into four distinct deception planes: transport, service protocol, vulnerability surface, and agentic session.
Includes a provenance plane that links planted honeypot credentials directly to evidence of downstream model-mediated processing by adversaries.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables safe, low-cost measurement and threat intelligence gathering on public-facing AI inference APIs, vector databases, and agent gateways without exposing actual models or execution environments to risk.

security.title: SEAL: Sealed Queries for Local Sanitization against Indirect Prompt Injection

summary.tldr: SEAL is an offline-learned soft prompt and token-scoring defense that sanitizes untrusted tool outputs via localized deletion using a frozen task model without generating defense tokens or using separate verifiers.
key_points: Constructs scoring queries from trusted initial context and a learned soft prompt, keeping the reference independent of inspected tool text.
Scores tokens without context-wide normalization and applies preservation regularization during localized deletion to retain task-relevant evidence.
Reduces attack success rate on AgentDojo from 34.6% to 0.1% while increasing joint task completion from 51.4% to 77.5%.
Requires approximately 127x fewer defense-related tokens than PISanitizer and demonstrates cross-backbone transferability.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables lightweight, highly effective mitigation of indirect prompt injections in resource-constrained local LLM agents without requiring secondary verifier models or heavy inference overhead.

security.title: Judging Before Propagation: Task-Graph Contextual Integrity for Multi-Agent Privacy

summary.tldr: Task-Graph Contextual Integrity (TG-CI) formalizes multi-agent privacy by evaluating information disclosure across stateful workflow graphs before propagation rather than judging local transfers in isolation.
key_points: TG-CI models workflows as Multi-Agent Task Graphs (MATGs) to evaluate privacy against an item's intended downstream propagation scope and recipient disclosure histories.
Implements two enforcement policies: Full-Scope (requires admissibility across the complete downstream graph) and Auto-Region (confines items to maximal admissible regions via frontier gates).
Evaluated on MAPLE-Bench, a new 144-case benchmark testing variations in MATG topology, disclosure history, compromised agents, and privacy policies.
Reduces mean unauthorized disclosures by 85.8-94.1% compared to Local-History CI baselines while preserving 93.6-96.1% of task accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents privacy leaks in complex multi-agent workflows where individual information transfers appear benign in isolation but breach confidentiality when propagated downstream.

security.title: Systematic Evaluation of Adversarial Jailbreaking Attacks and Defenses Across Seven Large Language Models

summary.tldr: A systematic evaluation of seven LLMs and four defenses reveals obfuscation attacks are the most effective (54.3% mean ASR), while self-reminder prompting provides the most robust defense.
key_points: Obfuscation attacks achieved a mean Attack Success Rate (ASR) of 54.3% across all models and bypassed every evaluated model with non-zero success.
Model size does not correlate with adversarial robustness (Spearman r = -0.57, p = 0.18), and vulnerability profiles vary widely even within the same architecture family.
Self-reminder prompting reduced ASR from 44% to 10% on Mistral-7B and from 48% to 5% on Llama-3.1-8B with zero false positives and no extra inference cost.
The study systematically benchmarked five attack types against open-weight and API models including Llama-3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.2-3B, Mistral-7B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma2-9B, and Phi-4-14B.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that scaling model size does not inherently grant security against jailbreaks, while highlighting self-reminder prompting as a cost-free, highly effective defense.

security.title: REALM: Identifying Minimal Task Assets for LLM Agents

summary.tldr: REALM enforces least privilege in LLM agents by dynamically building asset dependency graphs and isolating execution using task-specific Partial APIs and containers.
key_points: Uses a dependency graph to represent task assets and applies source-scoped selection to safely authorize assets discovered at runtime.
Separates asset discovery from authorization using a REALM Builder to manage grants and a Partial API Manager to expose resource-bound APIs inside a Task Container.
Tested on AgentDyn across 60 clean and 560 injected tasks using the qwen3.5-flash base model.
Reduces the attack success rate (ASR) of prompt injections from 16.6% to 0.2% while completing 40.0% of clean tasks and 36.4% of injected tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It mitigates prompt injection risks by preventing LLM agents from accessing redundant system resources and files during task execution.

security.title: Appreciation Teaches Unauthorized Execution: Self-Evolution Degrades the Robustness of Personal Agents to Indirect Prompt Injection

summary.tldr: Self-evolution mechanisms in personal agents degrade robustness against indirect prompt injection, increasing attack success rates after learning from user feedback.
key_points: Evaluated two self-evolution approaches: skill evolution and reinforcement learning from user feedback.
Tested using a two-phase framework: an adaptation phase with authorized tasks in external content and a test phase with unauthorized injected tasks.
Skill evolution increased the average Attack Success Rate (ASR) over the base agent by 14.0 to 48.8 percentage points.
Reinforcement learning evolution increased the average ASR over the base agent by 3.0 to 39.3 percentage points.
summary.why_it_matters: User-driven agent personalization inadvertently teaches systems to execute unauthorized third-party instructions hidden in external data, creating a severe security vulnerability.

security.title: Tracking AI adoption in North Korean threat actor tradecraft

summary.tldr: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has documented North Korean threat actors expanding AI integration to accelerate targeting, social engineering, malware development, and operational scaling while remaining human-directed.
key_points: Jade Sleet, Coral Sleet, and Jasper Sleet have reached an established stage of AI adoption across all operational workflows.
Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet are leveraging the open-source agentic AI penetration testing framework ARTEX in active operations.

Operational accelerations include Jade Sleet launching campaigns through three front companies in one week, Onyx Sleet generating dozens of lures in minutes, and Coral Sleet trojanizing private source code repositories.

Threat actors use AI as a force multiplier for existing objectives—including financial theft, intelligence collection, and supply chain targeting—rather than shifting motivations or achieving full autonomy.
summary.why_it_matters: Defenders must account for AI-accelerated cyber operations where threat actors rapidly generate lures, develop malware, and scale infrastructure without changing their underlying target profiles.

security.title: PCM: A Proof-Carrying Message Protocol for Verifiable Multi-Agent Communication

summary.tldr: Proof-Carrying Messages (PCM) is a cryptographic multi-agent communication protocol where messages carry Merkle inclusion proofs signed by external attesting signers, ensuring claims are verified offline independently of the sender's self-report.
key_points: Uses append-only Merkle log inclusion proofs signed by uncontrollable attesting signers, yielding three-valued verification outcomes: proven, unproven, or failed.
Restricts authority propagation through cryptographic grant chains that originate from recorded human approvals and can only narrow in scope.
Defines four claim types, a typed caveat algebra, replay rules, and strict readings to enforce deterministic verification across independent implementations.

Evaluated on a benchmark of 926 real-run messages (712 lies across 16 classes); PCM accepted only 10 stale-evidence lies (1.4% false-positive rate) at ~1 ms verification latency, outperforming six existing protocols.
summary.why_it_matters: PCM prevents prompt-injected agents from laundering fabricated facts or authority across multi-agent systems by decoupling message content verification from channel-level authentication.

security.title: FlipJev: Fast Black-Box Red Teaming Finds Universal Adversarial Suffixes for Typed Decision Models

summary.tldr: FlipJev is a fast, query-based black-box attack that finds short universal adversarial suffixes capable of flipping typed decision model outputs without using an attacker language model.
key_points: Evaluated Jev, a representative typed decision model, across 12 datasets covering various data types and application scenarios.
Jev demonstrated resistance to common prompt injections, maintaining correct answers across 10,240 paired tests.
FlipJev finds short suffixes within minutes that flip confident model answers, with a single dataset-specific suffix flipping 43% of unseen documents.
Generated adversarial suffixes transfer across distinct tasks, with a single suffix from one task successfully flipping 90-100% of samples in other tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating typed decision models requires strict adaptive attacks, as high cross-task transferability of universal suffixes poses a significant security risk to multi-task decision systems.

security.title: Where You Inject Matters: The Trust Region Effect in LLM Agents

summary.tldr: Researchers identify the trust region effect in LLM agents, demonstrating that attack success rates for indirect prompt injections vary based on where malicious instructions are placed within an environment.
key_points: Evaluated injection placements across three long-horizon agentic testbeds spanning tool use, coding, and daily workflows.
Observed that a GPT-5.4-powered agent executes unsafe instructions in repository documentation files (README/TODO) 2.6 times more frequently than in code or data files.
Developed learning-based attacker models that optimize both the content and the environmental placement of indirect prompt injections.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that LLM security defenses must account for uneven implicit trust across environment surfaces rather than focusing solely on inspecting raw text content.

security.title: CARI: Cross-Boundary Adversarial Runtime Injection in Coding-Agent Workflows

summary.tldr: CARI is a novel attack exploiting authority mismatch by embedding malicious instructions in peer-controlled runtime feedback, causing coding agents to execute unauthorized local actions.
key_points: Exploits authority mismatch where a compromised peer component has diagnostic authority to report state but lacks action authority over the victim's local environment.
Instantiates ten attacks across four programming languages, achieving a 94.8% (2,845/3,000) success rate across five code-capable models.
Transfers to commercial product-level agents, demonstrating a 61.3% attack success rate on Codex and 58.7% on Claude Code.
Evaluated defenses show a strict security-utility trade-off: generic prompt warnings fail, while explicit policies cause significant over-refusal of legitimate actions.
summary.why_it_matters: Multi-agent and collaborative coding environments are vulnerable to severe compromise via standard runtime feedback channels, and current prompt-level defenses fail to secure them without degrading utility.

infra.title: Lend and borrow resources across teams with AWS Batch’s quota management for SageMaker Training jobs

summary.tldr: AWS Batch introduces quota management for Amazon SageMaker Training jobs, enabling multi-team resource allocation, automated lending and borrowing of idle GPU capacity, and job preemption.
key_points: Quota shares act as virtual queues nested within job queues, allowing administrators to set compute limits and define sharing strategies: RESERVE, LEND, or LEND_AND_BORROW.
Cross-share preemption automatically reclaims lent capacity when new workloads arrive in the original lending quota share.
Priority-based in-share preemption preempts lower-priority jobs in SCHEDULED, STARTING, or RUNNING states to allow higher-priority jobs to execute immediately.
Configuration requires a Scheduling Policy containing a quotaSharePolicy and a Service Environment, supported via the SageMaker Python SDK v3.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates manual coordination and custom queuing overhead by automatically maximizing shared GPU cluster utilization while guaranteeing capacity for prioritized workloads across teams.

summary.tldr: AWS announced deployment patterns for NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120B-parameter hybrid Mamba-Transformer MoE multimodal model, on Amazon EKS, EKS Auto Mode, and SageMaker HyperPod EKS.
key_points: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL uses a hybrid Mamba-2, MoE, and attention architecture with a RADIO vision encoder, activating 12B of its 120B total parameters per token up to a 1M token context.
The model includes a recursively shared Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) head to support native speculative decoding.
Minimum vLLM hardware requirements range from 1 NVIDIA B300/GB300 GPU (for NVFP4) up to 16 H100 GPUs (for BF16).
Reference deployment infrastructure uses Amazon ECR for container images, Amazon FSx for Lustre for shared model weights, and EFA networking across GPU nodes.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables developers to deploy a high-context, open-weights multimodal model optimized for low-memory long-sequence inference on AWS-managed Kubernetes infrastructure.

infra.title: Day 0 support for Mistral Large 4 on vLLM

summary.tldr: vLLM announced day-0 support for Mistral Large 4, introducing optimizations for its native MoE multimodal architecture across NVIDIA Blackwell, AMD ROCm, and TPU hardware using Model Runner V2.
key_points: Mistral Large 4 integrates sparse MLA, a DSA top-k indexer, cross-layer KV sharing (nine NoPE layers reuse layer 35's KV cache), and a built-in DSpark speculative decoding drafter.
Per token KV cache footprint is 47,136 bytes (41,328 for MLA latent and 5,808 for the indexer), requiring 8 ranks via Decode Context Parallelism (DCP) for long contexts.
The model is deployed via Model Runner V2 (MRV2) with breakable CUDA graphs, supporting NVFP4 and FP8 quantizations.

NVFP4 decoding on Blackwell provides 1.08–1.19x faster decoding per token compared to FP8 without speculative decoding (1.18–1.22x with DSpark) while retaining performance within a -0.3 mean point margin.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables immediate, highly optimized production serving and speculative decoding for Mistral's latest 1T-class native multimodal model with minimal quality degradation and lower memory usage.

summary.tldr: Spawn is using autonomous Fable-class AI agent swarms spending over $3M monthly in tokens to continuously write, test, and ship live code updates to its multiplayer game world hourly.
key_points: Agent swarms run continuous deployment where missing an hourly production ship is treated as a SEV-0 incident to maintain agent coherence.

Fable 5 and 5.1 models enabled this level of autonomy, whereas Opus 5.5 failed to meet requirements and GPT-6 Astra broke functionality by disabling features during a security review.

summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates an extreme model of autonomous agentic engineering, using games as a low-stakes environment to push the boundaries of self-healing, continuous AI-driven software development.
